entity.name: Elixpo
entity.description: Elixpo is an open-source project foundry in India, a Udyam-registered MSME (UDYAM-WB-07-0152337). It builds FaleraOS and the Elixpo Falera Badge: open hardware, open software and the research behind them, all released under open licences. Team: Ayushman Bhattacharya (founder), Anwesha Chakraborty and Vivek Yadav (co-founders), and Nihal Gazi (maintainer).

projects.name: FaleraOS and the Elixpo Falera Badge
projects.description: FaleraOS is an open-source MicroPython operating system for the Elixpo Falera Badge, an open-hardware ESP32-S3 conference badge with a 2.8-inch touch screen, eight buttons, IR, a motion sensor, a speaker and microSD. It has an app SDK, an on-device App Store, over-the-air updates, a command-line tool (falera-cli) and RV565, a video format for small displays described in arXiv:2610.35935. The hardware is OSHWA-certified (IN000107) under CERN-OHL-P-2.0 and the software is MIT. Formerly OreoOS.

channels.description: The Falera Badge fundraiser on Elixpo Pay (UPI, cards and netbanking, in INR).

plans.name: The first five founder boards
plans.description: Bare PCBs from JLCPCB and parts from LCSC for the first five badges, paid out of pocket so far; the fundraiser's goal. Every price is in circuit/elixpo/BOM_COST.md.

plans.name: One badge
plans.description: The parts for one complete badge at the prices paid in November 2026 (board share, LCSC parts and shipping, display, battery and module), from circuit/elixpo/BOM_COST.md.

plans.name: Four months: the final version 2 board
plans.description: Four months, ₹2,50,000, to make the version 2 board final so every board after it works first time. Month 1: the first PCB badges running FaleraOS and a public build guide. Month 2: touch, audio and an app tutorial. Month 3: the final version 2 board. Month 4: 10 badges built and tested on it, and two workshops. Each milestone is reported in the repository; terms in pitch-deck/SPONSORSHIP.md.

plans.name: Maintainer stipends
plans.description: Four maintainers × ₹7,500 a month for four months (₹1,20,000), paid by milestone.

plans.name: The final version 2 board
plans.description: The fixes found on the first five boards, fabrication and assembly of version 2, and 10 badges built and tested on it.

plans.name: Two workshops
plans.description: Kits, travel and documentation for two build-and-code workshops: everyone builds a badge and publishes an app.

plans.name: Test equipment
plans.description: A hot-air station, a bench power supply and a logic analyser for bringing up and testing every board.

history.description: Income: the community fundraiser, ₹872 from 16 people as of 21 November 2026. Expenses: the first five PCBs (JLCPCB, ₹4,122) and their parts (LCSC, ₹4,063), paid by the maintainers.
